Package neqsim.pvtsimulation.reservoirproperties.materialbalance

Class GeneralizedMaterialBalance

java.lang.Object
neqsim.pvtsimulation.reservoirproperties.materialbalance.GeneralizedMaterialBalance
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class GeneralizedMaterialBalance extends Object implements Serializable
Generalized two-component reservoir material balance including vaporized oil.

Implements the conservation basis of Walsh (1995), doi:10.2118/95-01-07. Unlike a conventional black-oil balance, both solution gas Rs and vaporized oil Rv are retained. Observations can come from measured history or a forward tank simulation. PVT must be independently calibrated and evaluated on the appropriate depletion/separator path. This class neither tunes an EOS nor infers aquifer influx from pressure alone.

All surface quantities use Sm3 on ONE fixed separator/stock-tank basis; formation volume factors use reservoir m3/Sm3. Net cumulative production means produced minus injected, from the initial state. Aquifer influx is already in reservoir m3 and must not be multiplied by Bw again. Injection is valid only when its component amounts are represented by the same two surface pseudo-components and the PVT path remains representative. Strong composition changes require full compositional simulation.

Fits minimize unweighted reservoir-volume residuals, not pressure errors. Scaled QR least squares and an SVD condition-number gate reject non-identifiable fits. Results are hydrocarbon volumes in place, not recoverable reserves or confidence intervals. Near-critical Rs*Rv approaching one is explicitly rejected.

  • Method Details

    • addObservation

      public void addObservation(BlackOilPVTTable.Record pvt, double netOilProduced, double netGasProduced, double netWaterProduced, double waterInflux, double expansionFraction)
      Adds an aligned historical pressure/PVT/cumulative-production observation.

      The optional rock/connate-water support is specified as a dimensionless expansion fraction of INITIAL hydrocarbon reservoir volume. In the linear small-compressibility approximation it is (cf + Swi*cw)/(1-Swi)*(pi-p), with compressibilities in 1/bar. Use zero for a rigid tank with constant water volume. The fraction can be negative under repressurization; influx can be negative for efflux.

      Parameters:
      pvt - PVT at measured average reservoir pressure on the calibrated path
      netOilProduced - cumulative stock-tank oil produced minus injected (Sm3)
      netGasProduced - cumulative standard gas produced minus injected (Sm3)
      netWaterProduced - cumulative standard water produced minus injected (Sm3)
      waterInflux - cumulative aquifer influx (reservoir m3), excluding injected water
      expansionFraction - rock/connate-water expansion per initial hydrocarbon volume
